Read in parallel (HANDOFF.md uses **read-from-end strategy** — SSP-01 v6.5.0; monolítico newest-first, **~10k+ linhas e crescendo** — rode o `wc -l` do pre-flight, NÃO assuma um total fixo):
- `HANDOFF.md` with `limit=30` → FIRST ACTION FOR NEXT AGENT + o topo do Task State (a 1ª linha do Task State = a fase mais recém-selada; é o que importa).
- ⚠️ **TOKEN-CAP GUARD (aprendido 2026-07-19):** as linhas do Task State e dos Records são **parágrafos densos (2-4k chars cada)** — uma janela de 55-400 linhas pode **estourar o teto de 25k tokens do Read** e falhar. **Regra:** leia em janelas de **≤150 linhas**; se o Read retornar erro de token-cap, **corte a janela pela metade** e repita. Nunca insista numa janela grande "porque o doc manda".
- Para o Record mais recente (últimas 1-2 fases seladas): comece em `offset ≈ (total − 40)` com `limit=20` (pega a última linha do Task State) e depois leia o bloco `## … Record` mais novo em janelas ≤150 linhas subindo. As seções de sufixo (Pending Actions · GraphRAG State · Infrastructure · Key Files) ficam **no `CLAUDE.md`/`sprint-priorities`**, não no fim do HANDOFF.md — priorize aquelas.
- 📌 **Se `wc -l HANDOFF.md` > ~4000:** o arquivo está pesado demais p/ pickup eficiente — sinalize nos ALERTAS que o `/handoff` deveria **arquivar Records antigos** (ver Phase 5 do seal). Um HANDOFF.md enxuto (Task State + ~12 Records recentes) é o alvo.
- `CLAUDE.md` (architecture rules, data flow, key files — incluindo MCORCH Master Execution Protocol + Survival Laws link)
- `.claude/context/sprint-priorities.md` (sprint goal, 4Cs snapshot, top gaps)
- `/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-home-gcrUX-htdocs-constellation-orchestra/memory/MEMORY.md` (memory index)

> ⚠️ **Auditoria histórica de seals antigos:** usar `Read` com offset arbitrário em HANDOFF.md (fora do fluxo padrão de pickup). Ordering newest-first: seal mais antigo ≈ linha 2805, seal mais recente logo após linha 71. Cada `## <Phase> Record (YYYY-MM-DD)` marca um seal. ### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ "$slug" = "security" ]; then
    required_sec=(00-deepsearch-blueprint 01-brd-security 02-srs-secure-spec 03-sdd-hardening-architecture 04-fmea-security)
    missing=()
    for doc in "${required_sec[@]}"; do
      [ -f "docs/bok/security/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
    done
    [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ security — BoK complete (ciso-4-artifact)" || echo "⚠️ security — missing: ${missing[*]}"
    continue
  fi
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

If the user mentions working on a **new module / complex feature / integration / architectural change**:
- Check whether `docs/bok/<expected-slug>/` exists with all 9 docs.
- If missing: surface in the **ALERTAS** section as a critical block per CLAUDE.md MCORCH Master Execution Protocol.
- Recommend `/bok-scribe <idea summary>` before any code is written.

## Fase 7 (opcional) — PMO handoff (`pmo-curator`)

Depois de entregar o brief, **ofereça** disparar o PMO tático: a skill `pmo-curator` lê o mesmo estado, aplica MAPE-K de PROGRESSO e materializa os próximos passos priorizados em `NEXT-STEPS.md` (un-gated vs gated, dependências, deadlines, comando exato de cada passo executável).

- **Quando oferecer:** sempre que o Sovereign, após o brief, pedir "os próximos passos / o que atacar primeiro / priorize o backlog / gere o plano".
- **Como:** invocar a skill `pmo-curator` (ou delegar ao subagente homônimo). Ela é **plan-only** — não executa nada.
- **Fronteira:** o `pmo-curator` é o loop de PROGRESSO; **não** é o guardião MAPE-K (loop de confiabilidade — infra/incidentes). SOP: `docs/processes/pmo-curator.md`.

Não force — o `/handson` continua entregando o brief como sempre; o PMO é uma camada de planejamento opcional por cima.

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

> ### Documentário informativo · usa o método SEM anunciar o produto · motion-first (Veo só no apresentador)

> 
> ## 1. CABEÇALHO
> 
> | Campo | Valor |
> |---|---|
> | **Título principal** | A IA saiu da jaula esta semana (e a conta chegou) |
> | **Alt. A/B** | Uma IA invadiu 3 empresas de verdade — e ninguém mandou |
> | **Thumb / headline** | `SAIU DA JAULA` (ciano, texto ≤7% da área) |
> | **Duração-alvo** | 8–10 min |
> | **Formato** | 16:9 master YouTube · pt-BR · compilado semanal de novidades |
> | **Atos** | 4 + gancho + CTA |

> | **Voz** | Narração 100% IVC do Sovereign (ElevenLabs `eleven_v3`, tom NOVIDADES). Apresentador = áudio Veo nativo. A voz NUNCA troca. |
> | **ORO** | Operator = Agent · Reviewer = Sovereign (parecer por peça) · Owner = Sovereign (marca/canal/saldo) |

> **Regras invioláveis:** gancho falado ≤7s · nenhum número não-ancorado (todo dado tem fonte no brief) · toda claim de terceiro dita como *"segundo a Anthropic / segundo o Financial Times"* · quebra de padrão a cada 30-45s · fecho PRESCRITIVO ("o que baixar primeiro, o que ignorar") · CTA de engajamento · QA A/V sync obrigatório antes do master.

> **Por que este tema e não o EP05:** o EP05 apresenta o método/produto — vai ao ar depois que o método estiver provado com outras pessoas. Este episódio APLICA o método sem falar dele.

## 🤖 Claude *(22:16:12)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I'm examining the motion-bridge rendering pipeline and how it currently outputs visuals through Playwright and FFmpeg with deterministic frame seeking. The user is asking for VFX-quality 3D motion design, but the existing engine is built on 2D SVG and CSS animations driven by mathematical seek functions. To achieve that 3D visual fidelity within the constraints, I'd need to integrate WebGL or Three.js to render deterministically frame-by-frame based on seek positions rather than relying on the current 2D approach.

Beyond pure 3D, there are advanced 2D-3D hybrid techniques I could layer in — CSS 3D transforms with perspective, depth-of-field effects through layered blur, parallax scrolling, bokeh particles, volumetric lighting, glass refraction using backdrop filters, chromatic aberration, film grain, and motion blur via temporal supersampling. The post-processing pipeline already exists in FFmpeg, so I could extend it with bloom, vignette, and additional grading. The real pro-level quality comes from temporal supersampling to create smooth motion blur, easing curves based on animation principles like anticipation and overshoot, and kinetic typography staging.

The user also wants a self-contained loop that doesn't require ongoing input and can scale into a product vision around templates and a SaaS model. For this session, there's a concrete first deliverable: disabling the `auth_social_login_visible` flag on TikTok, which is already approved and unblocked.

Beyond that, the bigger work is a Motion Design v3 upgrade with a full VFX 3D engine and learning loop. I'm planning to use a multi-workflow approach with research agents exploring professional motion design techniques from studios like Kurzgesagt and Vox, social media retention mechanics from creators like MrBeast, and the technical foundations for deterministic WebGL rendering.

Then I'll have a synthesis agent pull together a "Motion Doctrine v3" with a gap analysis against the current engine. For implementation, I need to split the work across separate modules in the motion/vfx directory to avoid file conflicts when multiple agents work in parallel, then integrate everything back together.

I should start with Workflow A since everything else depends on it, but I can run that in the background while I handle the TikTok flag and review more context. I also need to check the BoK gate — this engine upgrade counts as a complex architectural change, so I'll need to file an Amendment under the spaces-evolution docs.

For Workflow A, I'm planning two phases of reconnaissance: internal agents examining the current motion system and existing EP06 hooks, then external agents researching VFX studios, social retention techniques, deterministic 3D rendering, cinematography, and kinetic typography. After that, I'll bring in a critic agent to validate the findings.

</details>

> export function extractBigNumber(text: string): { value: number; label: string } | null {

> 
>     let scale = 1;

>     // com unidade de escala vence sem unidade; empatado, o maior
>     if (!best || (scaled && !best.scaled) || ((scaled === best.scaled) && value > best.value)) {
>       best = { value, label: m[0].trim(), scaled };
>     }
>   }
>   return best ? { value: best.value, label: best.label } : null;
> }

## 🤖 Claude *(22:21:04)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I found the culprit — there's an actual NUL byte (0x00) embedded in the template string within `sceneSeed`, which appeared as a space when displayed in the terminal. This binary character is causing the file to be classified as binary, which explains why `grep -r` isn't finding matches.

The NUL works as a separator for the FNV hash calculation, so there's no runtime bug, but it's a fragility risk: any tool that normalizes or re-encodes the file could silently drop or convert the NUL, changing every scene seed and altering motion renders without warning. The fix is to replace the literal NUL with an explicit `\u0000` escape sequence — this produces the exact same hash input and keeps the file as plain text, with zero visual change to the output.

I'll write a small Node script to do the byte replacement precisely, then verify the fix by computing the scene seed before and after the patch to prove the hashes are identical.

</details>

That's a net gain in visual quality while freeing up computational budget for real visual effects.

To implement this, I'll either pre-render each blob as its own blurred sprite and translate them individually (letting the compositor cache the textures), or use a radial-gradient approximation to simulate the soft falloff of a blurred blob without the performance cost.
